**Analysis:**

**Test image observations:** A mature mango leaf (still green) with dark brownish-black patches scattered across the surface. The dark areas appear superficial — like a coating on the leaf rather than sunken/raised lesions. The darkening is most pronounced on the right/lower portion of the leaf.

**Candidate elimination:**
- **Die_Back**: Severely withered, entirely brown/curled leaves — doesn't match (leaf is still green and flat)
- **Cutting_Weevil**: Stripped shoots with triangular cut remnants — doesn't match
- **Gall_Midge**: Small round blister galls on leaves — doesn't match (no raised bumps visible)
- **Anthracnose**: Young tan/yellow leaves with dark margin lesions — doesn't match (leaf is mature and green)
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Angular spots with raised margins, necrotic leaf edges — doesn't match
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White/powdery spots — doesn't match (dark patches, not white)
- **Sooty_Mould**: Black superficial encrustation on leaf surface growing on honeydew — **matches perfectly**: dark patchy coating on otherwise green mature leaf, identical pattern to Sooty Mould reference images (especially bottom-right panel showing scattered dark patches on green leaf)
